modules.name: Introduction and Basic Terms in Thermodynamics

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
• Thermodynamics: Studies energy transformations in physical and chemical processes.

Thermodynamics terms:-  Universe = System + Surrounding

• Boundary : Anything which separates system and surrounding.

Types of Boundary:- Real & Imaginary , Rigid & Flexible , Conducting & Non-Conducting

• Types of System :-

Open system : mass and energy exchange (eg. Open vessel , All living systems , Classroom, earth.)

Closed system : energy exchange but mass not exchange (eg. Closed vessel , Glowing bulb, tube light , A satellite in orbit.)

Isolated system : neither matter nor energy can be exchanged (eg. thermos flask.)

• State of the System :-

State Function : eg. E, H, S, G, T, P, V etc.

Path function : eg. Work done (w), heat (q)

• Thermodynamic properties :-

Intensive properties : independent of quantity or size of matter (eg. Density (d), All concentration terms(M, N) etc.)

Extensive properties : dependent on quantity or size of matter (eg. Volume (V), Number of moles (n) , Mass (M) etc.)

Special Points :

• The ratio of two extensive properties indicates the intensive property.
    • An extensive property can be converted into intensive property when it is defined for unit amount of the substance.
    • Intensive properties of a substance are non-additive in nature while extensive properties are additive in nature.

blocks.title: Types of Thermodynamic Processes
blocks.text:
• Isothermal Process (n, T = constant)

The temperature of the system during the entire process remains constant, i.e. (ΔT = 0)

For ideal gas in Isothermal process ΔE = 0 and ΔH = 0

• Isobaric Process (n, P=constant)

The pressure of the system during the entire process remains constant, i.e. (ΔP = 0)

Process in an open system is isobaric in nature.

• Isochoric Process (n, V = constant)

Volume remains constant i.e.(ΔV = 0)

Process in a closed system is isochoric in nature.

• Adiabatic Process (n = constant, q = 0)

No exchange of heat between the system and surroundings takes place during the entire process, i.e.  q = 0

The system is thermally insulated by keeping the system in an insulated container.

• Cyclic Process

In a cyclic process, change in all state functions will be zero. i.e. ΔE = 0,ΔH = 0, ΔP = 0, ΔT = 0

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• Misidentifying processes, such as considering adiabatic as constant temperature.
  • Confusing State Function with Path function and Intensive properties with Extensive properties
  • Error: Not distinguishing between different types of systems when applying thermodynamic principles.

blocks.title: Additional Guidelines
blocks.text:
• Use PV diagrams for visualization.
  • Identify the process type to apply the correct formula during problem-solving.
  • Strategy: Identify system type (open, closed, isolated) to apply the correct energy balance equation.

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Internal Energy (E/U) :Internal energy of a system is defined as the sum of different energies

We can only calculate the change in internal energy of the system (ΔE) by using an instrument which is called as Bomb calorimeter. In Bomb calorimeter reactions are carried out at constant volume.

blocks.title: Formulas & Mathematical Relations
blocks.text:
Work: -   w = –PexternalΔV = – Δng RT (In reaction)

Internal Energy: -  ΔE = Ef – Ei

ΔE = $E_P–E_R$ (In reaction)

blocks.title: Internal Energy
blocks.text:
Sign convention     ΔE is + ve if Ef > Ei /  Ep > ER

ΔE is – ve if Ef < Ei /  Ep < ER

Units of heat & work :

1 Cal = 4.184 J ~ 4.2 J

1 L-atm = 101.3 J = 24.206 Cal = 101.3 × $10^7$erg

• Work in rigid vessel is zero because volume remains constant.

• Work during free expansion of an ideal gas in vacuum is zero, because Pext is zero.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• Confusing sign convention and unit conversion.
  • To avoid confusion, remember the value of R as:
8.314 J/mol·K or 2 cal/mol·K.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question: Determine the work done by a gas when it expands at constant pressure of 2 atm from a volume of 5 L to 10 L.
blocks.prompt: Determine the work done by a gas when it expands at constant pressure of 2 atm from a volume of 5 L to 10 L.

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
The mathematical form of first law of thermodynamics can be expressed as follows

$\Delta E = q + W$

Here q is the energy given to the system and w is the work done on the system; $\Delta E$ is change in internal energy.

The sum of internal energy and pressure volume (PV) energy is known as enthalpy.

ΔH = ΔE + Δ(PV)

blocks.title: Formulas & Mathematical Relations
blocks.text:
Conclusions from the First Law of Thermodynamics:

• During isothermal process of an ideal gas (ΔE = 0): +q = – w or –q = +w

• During isochoric process (ΔV = 0): $ΔE = q_v $

• During adiabatic process (q = 0): ΔE = w
    • During Cyclic process (ΔE = 0):  +q = – w or –q = +w
    • During Isobaric process (ΔP = 0): ΔH =  qp

Enthalpy

ΔH = ΔE +  Δng RT

qp =   $q_v$ +  Δng RT

blocks.title: Dependence on path
blocks.text:
In isochoric process heat is independent of path.

In adiabatic process work is independent of path.

In isobaric process heat is independent of path.

if  Δng= 0  →  ΔH = ΔE

if  Δng> 0  →  ΔH > ΔE

if  Δng< 0  →  ΔH < ΔE

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question: Calculate the change in internal energy for a system where 500 J of heat is added, and the system does 200 J of work.
blocks.prompt: Calculate the change in internal energy for a system where 500 J of heat is added, and the system does 200 J of work.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.question:
At 27°C the internal energy change of reaction

$\text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \text{Cl}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{HCl}(\text{g})
$ is 2Cal. What is the enthalpy change of this reaction ?
blocks.prompt:

$\text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \text{Cl}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{HCl}(\text{g})
$ is 2Cal. What is the enthalpy change of this reaction ?

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• Confusing sign conventions of work done by the system with work done on the system.
  • Misapplying ΔU=Q−W to systems that are not closed or under non-standard conditions.
  • Confusing enthalpy change (ΔH) with internal energy change (ΔU).
  • Assuming ΔH=ΔU without considering PΔV work, especially in non-ideal conditions.
Note:

Ensure to review and practice problems where ΔU=q+W is applied, especially for isochoric and isobaric processes. Understanding the direction of heat and work flow is crucial in solving thermodynamics problems effectively.

Focus on understanding the conditions under which each formula is applicable, such as constant pressure for enthalpy changes, to avoid common errors in calculations.

modules.name: Heat Capacity / Work Done in Different Process

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Heat capacity (C): Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of given amount of a substance by 1°C or 1K is called heat capacity.

Molar heat capacity (Cm): Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 mole of substance by 1°C or 1 K is called as molar heat capacity.

Specific heat capacity (c): Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 g of substance by 1°C or 1K is called as specific heat capacity.

blocks.title: Relation between CP and CV for 1 mole of an ideal gas :
blocks.text:
• Mayer's formula: - $C_{p,m}$$-  C_{v,m}  = R$

• Poisson's ratio: -  $\frac{C_p}{C_v} = \gamma$

Work done in the reversible isothermal process:

• Wrev. = –2.303 nRT log10  $\frac{V_2}{V_1}$

• Wrev. = –2.303 nRT log10  $\frac{P_1}{P_2}$

Work done in the isothermal irreversible process

$W_{irrev} = –P_{ext}(V_2 - V_1)$

Work done in a reversible adiabatic process:

• w = n Cv,m $\left( T_2 - T_1 \right) $

  • $W = \frac{nR}{\gamma - 1} \left( T_2 - T_1 \right) = W = \frac{P_2 V_2 - P_1 V_1}{\gamma - 1}$

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question: 5 moles of oxygen are heated at constant volume from 10°C to 20°C. What will be the change in the internal energy of gas? The molar heat capacity of oxygen at constant pressure, CP = 7.03 Cal mol–1 K–1 and R=2 Cal mol–1 K–1
blocks.prompt: 5 moles of oxygen are heated at constant volume from 10°C to 20°C. What will be the change in the internal energy of gas? The molar heat capacity of oxygen at constant pressure, CP = 7.03 Cal mol–1 K–1 and R=2 Cal mol–1 K–1

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.question: At 27°C, one mole of an ideal gas compressed isothermally and reversibly from a pressure of 2 atm to 10 atm. Calculate E and q in calorie.
blocks.prompt: At 27°C, one mole of an ideal gas compressed isothermally and reversibly from a pressure of 2 atm to 10 atm. Calculate E and q in calorie.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• Confusing heat capacity with specific heat capacity.
  • Misapplying the equation for heat transfer.
  • Confusing reversible and irreversible work.
Note:

  • Heat capacity depends on the path and whether the process is at constant volume or constant pressure.
  • The work done in a reversible expansion process is larger than in an irreversible expansion for the same change in state.

modules.name: Entropy and the Second Law of Thermodynamics

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Spontaneous Process :

• The process which has a natural tendency to occur in a particular direction either of its own or after proper initiation under the given set of conditions.

Non–spontaneous Process:

• The process which does not occur on its own in a particular direction i.e. a process which does not have a natural tendency to occur in a particular direction either of its own or after initiation is called as non-spontaneous process.

Entropy (s):

• The thermodynamic quantity, which is used to measure degree of randomness or disorderness of the system is called as entropy.

• Entropy (s) Randomness or disorderness

blocks.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics (SLOT):
blocks.text:
• It states about the direction of flow of heat.
    • All natural processes in universe are irreversible process or natural processes are spontaneous process.
    • Due to spontaneous process entropy of universe is increasing continuously ie. entropy of an isolated system increases.

blocks.title: Formulas & Mathematical Relations
blocks.text:
Entropy (s) : $\Delta S = \frac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T}$

Case I: For an ideal gas reversible isothermal process;  $T_2 = T_1$

ΔS  = 2.303 nR log10  $\frac{V_2}{V_1}$ = ΔS = 2.303 nR log10 $\frac{P_1}{P_2}$

Case II: For an isochoric process $V_2 = V_1$

ΔS  = 2.303 nCV log10  $\frac{T_2}{T_1}$

Case III: For a reversible adiabatic process $q_{rev} = 0$

ΔS  = 0 (S constant)

Entropy remains constant so process is also known as isoentropic process.

Entropy change during phase transition :

  • Entropy of Fusion $\left[ S \right]_f$ : $\Delta S_f = \frac{\Delta H_f}{T}$
  • Entropy of vapourisation $\left[ S \right]_v$ : $\Delta S_v = \frac{\Delta H_v}{T}$
  • Entropy of sublimation $\left[ S \right]_s:\Delta S_s = \frac{\Delta H_s}{T}$

blocks.title: DATA
blocks.text:
The entropy of Universe :  $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{system}} + \Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$

Factors affecting the entropy of the system :

• Moles ↑  S ↑

  • Physical state : $S_{\text{solid}} < S_{\text{liquid}} < S_{\text{gas}}$
• T ↑ S ↑
    • P  ↓  S ↑
    • Mixture: S ↑

Some famous or extraordinary examples of entropy change :

• Entropy of graphite > Entropy of diamond.
    • Entropy is positive for dissolution process.
    • Entropy decreases due to precipitation.
    • On boiling of egg : Entropy increases
    • Stretching of rubber : Entropy decreases

Total entropy changes in reversible process: $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 0$

Total entropy changes in an irreversible process: $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = +\text{ve} \quad (\because T_2 > T_1)$

Spontaneity of a process in terms of total entropy change:

If $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = +\text{ive}$ (Spontaneous process)

If $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = –\text{ive}$ (Nonspontaneous process)

If $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 0$ (Process at equilibrium)

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question:
Which of the following processes are accompanied by increase of entropy :

(i) Dissolution of iodine in a solvent $\text{I}_2(s) \rightarrow \text{I}_2(aq.)$

(ii) HCl is added to AgNO3 and a precipitate of AgCl is obtained.

(iii) A partition is removed to allow two gases to mix.
blocks.prompt:
Which of the following processes are accompanied by increase of entropy :

(i) Dissolution of iodine in a solvent $\text{I}_2(s) \rightarrow \text{I}_2(aq.)$

(ii) HCl is added to AgNO3 and a precipitate of AgCl is obtained.

(iii) A partition is removed to allow two gases to mix.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.question: Calculate the change in entropy for the fusion of 1 mol of ice. The melting point of ice is 273K and molar enthalpy of fusion of ice = 6 kJ mol–1
blocks.prompt: Calculate the change in entropy for the fusion of 1 mol of ice. The melting point of ice is 273K and molar enthalpy of fusion of ice = 6 kJ mol–1

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
Misconception: Entropy is energy; it is actually a measure of energy dispersion.

Error: Assuming entropy decreases in all natural processes; it decreases locally but increases globally.

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
• Gibb's energy is defined at constant temperature and pressure to predict spontaneity of a process.

• Gibb's energy is a thermodynamic quantity which is used to measure the capacity of system to do useful work or Gibb's energy is that part of the total energy of system which can be converted into useful work.

blocks.title: Formulas & Mathematical Relations
blocks.text:
• Gibbs Energy

ΔG = ΔH - TΔS

• Relation between Gibb's energy change and non expansion work or useful work :

$\mathrm{W_{useful}} = –\Delta\mathrm{G}$

The decrease in Gibb's energy of system is equal to the non expansion work or useful work.

• Relation in between ΔG of system and
$\Delta S_{total}$ or Gibb's energy change and spontaneity :

$\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{sys}} + \left( -\frac{\Delta H_{\text{sys}}}{T} \right)$

$\Delta G_{\text{sys}} = - T \Delta S_{\text{total}}$

• Relationship between standard Gibb's energy change (ΔG°) and Equilibrium constant (Keq) :-

Keq = e -ΔG°/RT

ΔG° = – 2.303 RT log Kc

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question: For a reaction at 25°C enthalpy change (ΔH) and entropy change (ΔS) are –11.7×103 J mol–1 and –105 J mol–1 K–1 respectively. Find out whether this reaction is spontaneous or not.
blocks.prompt: For a reaction at 25°C enthalpy change (ΔH) and entropy change (ΔS) are –11.7×103 J mol–1 and –105 J mol–1 K–1 respectively. Find out whether this reaction is spontaneous or not.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.question:
Calculate the equilibrium constant for the reaction given below at 400K.

If ΔH°=77.2 kJmol-1 and ΔS° = 122 JK-1 mol-1

PCl5(g) ⎯→ PCl3(g) + Cl2(g)
blocks.prompt:
Calculate the equilibrium constant for the reaction given below at 400K.

If ΔH°=77.2 kJmol-1 and ΔS° = 122 JK-1 mol-1

PCl5(g) ⎯→ PCl3(g) + Cl2(g)

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
Misconception: Confusing ΔG with reaction rate; ΔG indicates spontaneity, not speed.

Misunderstanding: Spontaneous reaction (ΔG<0) does not always proceed rapidly; some are slow.

$\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{sys}} + \left( -\frac{\Delta H_{\text{sys}}}{T} \right)$

$\Delta G_{\text{sys}} = - T \Delta S_{\text{total}}$

• Relationship between standard Gibb's energy change (ΔG°) and Equilibrium constant (Keq) :-

Keq = e -ΔG°/RT

ΔG° = – 2.303 RT log Kc
